concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of powers of a variable with coefficients, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with i² = −1, with modulus, conjugation and unit-modulus phases e^{iθ}.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machines
concepts.gloss: A machine with a finite alphabet, finite control and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes whose heads each move at most one cell per step.

concepts.name: The n log n conjecture and multiplication history
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen conjectured that n log n is the optimal multiplication cost on multitape Turing machines; Schönhage–Strassen, Fürer and Harvey–van der Hoeven gave successively better upper bounds down to O(n log n).

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The normalized transform (F_q u)_k = (1/q) Σ_j u_j e^{−2πi jk/q} sending q complex values to their q frequency components.

evidence.quote: (F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of two length-q sequences viewed as polynomials modulo x^q − 1, so that indices wrap around cyclically.

evidence.quote: cyclic convolution on the product of the coordinate groups

concepts.name: Convolution theorem
concepts.gloss: The Fourier transform turns cyclic convolution into pointwise multiplication (up to normalization), so a convolution costs two forward transforms, a pointwise product and one inverse transform.

concepts.name: FFT butterflies (decimation in frequency)
concepts.gloss: The recursive FFT step that pairs entries z_k and z_{k+t/2}, replaces them by their half-sum and half-difference, multiplies one output by a root of unity and recurses on both halves.

evidence.quote: the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$ for

concepts.name: Integer multiplication as radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Splitting each integer into digits in a fixed radix turns the product into a convolution of the digit sequences, whose coefficients are then carried into binary.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Multidimensional (tensor) transform
concepts.gloss: The Fourier transform on a product of axes, applied as the tensor product of one-dimensional transforms along each axis.

evidence.quote: multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: An isomorphism sending a cyclic convolution of length S = s_1⋯s_d (pairwise coprime) to a convolution on d prime-length cyclic axes, implemented here by triangular controlled shifts.

evidence.quote: placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

concepts.name: Fixed-point and Gaussian dyadic arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Complex values stored as signed two's-complement integers times 2^{−p}; additions, halvings and multiplications by i are exact with enough guard bits, and truncation Q_p to the grid has error below √2·2^{−p}.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics,
\|Q_p z-z\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}

concepts.name: Linear contractions and error accumulation
concepts.gloss: A map that does not increase the maximum-modulus norm; applying contractions to approximate inputs never enlarges the input error, so errors of composed approximations add.

evidence.quote: A linear contraction propagates an input error without increasing it.

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven's identity expressing a prime-length Fourier transform through a power-of-two-length one via Gaussian-weighted contractions A and B_0; the two coordinate permutations are left inside the identity rather than sorted.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.
Resampling without executing the two permutations

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewrites a Fourier transform as two pointwise multiplications by a chirp phase around a cyclic convolution with the chirp, so the middle transform (with its target permutation) becomes a convolution.

concepts.name: Cancellation of the retained source permutation
concepts.gloss: The coordinate permutation retained in the resampling identity cancels across the two forward transforms, their pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform, leaving (u*v)/S².

evidence.quote: the source permutation retained during resampling cancels

concepts.name: Prime source lengths near powers of two
concepts.gloss: Choice of distinct primes s_i slightly below the power-of-two axis lengths t_i (using a prime-interval estimate) so that their product fills a fixed fraction of the padded box while each ratio t_i/s_i leaves room for resampling.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials of degree below r in which y^r = −1, so multiplying by a power of y shifts the coefficient list with sign changes.

evidence.quote: is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$
\mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)

concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomials, subject to the relation y^r + 1 = 0.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.name: Synthetic roots of unity
concepts.gloss: In the negacyclic ring, powers of y serve as roots of unity ω_t = y^{2r/t}, and multiplying by one is an exact signed shift of the coefficient list with no arithmetic.

evidence.quote: Powers of $y$ then serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes
Multiplication by $y^a$, for any integer $a$, permutes the coefficients and changes some signs

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A Fourier transform over the negacyclic ring (Nussbaumer–Quandalle) that uses powers of y as roots and is computed by butterflies, signed shifts and address rearrangements.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Coefficient phase twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r} turns cyclic convolution of length r into convolution modulo y^r + 1 (negative wrap), and untwisting restores the cyclic wrap.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing of polynomial products
concepts.gloss: Evaluating integer-coefficient polynomials at a large base B_0 packs them into integers so that one large integer multiplication yields all coefficients of the product, with signs handled by centered residues.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution
Signed packing and normalized ring multiplication

concepts.name: Array layout and elementary tape streams
concepts.gloss: Arrays stored in lexicographic address order on tape, with linear-time scans that permute digit positions, split into aligned streams, apply pointwise maps and merge them back.

evidence.quote: An array with address set $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.
Elementary stream operations

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shifts of an address field
concepts.gloss: A target address field is shifted cyclically by an offset computed from earlier control fields in linear time, which also gives multiplication by fixed units modulo q^b.

evidence.quote: Controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings

concepts.name: Three-element subset gates (copy, gather, scatter, side wires)
concepts.gloss: Fixed linear maps indexed by three-element subsets of {1..100} whose coefficients depend on intersection size; auxiliary side and center wires cancel the unwanted coefficients and are restored afterwards.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.
Alon's presentation of the Frankl--Wilson construction

concepts.name: Scratch-restoring bank-exchange network
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network of wires and gates that, in three stages, exchanges two banks of values with prescribed signs and restores every auxiliary scratch value whatever its initial content.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.

concepts.name: Frames: changing representation along a network
concepts.gloss: Arrays replace scalars on wires; each vertex has an invertible frame operator D_v, edges apply D_v D_u^{-1}, and pointwise linear gates commute with the common frame, so the whole network acts as D_out S D_in^{-1}.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.

concepts.name: Subspace labels and the rank deficit
concepts.gloss: Nested subspaces of a fixed bilinear space attached to gates and terminals make each edge cost its rank in smaller operations; the total s of these ranks is strictly less than W·m, where W is the wire count and m the label-space dimension.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
orthogonal residual

concepts.name: Recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: A call at parameter m·f uses s calls at parameter f on streams of volume V/W, so cost per volume obeys F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1} + O(1) with s/W < m, giving cost O(V e^τ) for some fixed τ < 1.

evidence.quote: This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.
F_0=O(1),\qquad F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1).

concepts.name: Lower triangular (Bruhat-type) factorization
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix A of rank a factors as E_1 Π E_2 with E_1, E_2 invertible lower triangular and Π a partial permutation matrix with a ones.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Cost of a rational matrix shear
concepts.gloss: The address map (H,D) ↦ (H + AD, D) of rank a is performed with exactly a interchanges of pairs of b-digit fields plus linear work, by factoring A and using three controlled updates around each swap.

evidence.quote: can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit

concepts.name: Address-chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: The first tape procedure: it swaps two disjoint address chunks of u bits in a complete array of volume V in time O(V u^τ) for a fixed τ < 1, internally using XOR combinations of intermediate data yet ending as an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian product.
Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.name: Phase frames and the C kernel
concepts.gloss: Over Gaussian dyadic values, the phase frame changes between binary subspace labels are products of two-point kernels aI + bX_v (a=(1+i)/2, b=(1−i)/2), one per orthonormal residual vector, and telescope to C^{⊗m} on every role.

evidence.quote: per vector in an orthonormal basis
C=H\mathsf SH=aI+bX

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: Adds (XORs) the same bit position of f address chunks of one field into another, using a few cyclic shifts of whole chunks and a correction of an explicitly bounded set of exceptional addresses.

evidence.quote: We implement a binary row addition on corresponding selected bits in two address chunks.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: The second tape procedure: applies H_0(u,v) = ((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) to one selected bit in each of up to d address chunks at once on polynomial records, in time O(V d^λ') for fixed λ' < 1, evaluated exactly and truncated once.

evidence.quote: simultaneously on selected coordinate bits of the numerical arrays.
the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$.

concepts.name: Tape layout of synthetic transforms
concepts.gloss: A layout placing the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive K-bit chunks so that simultaneous layers and chunk interchanges evaluate the synthetic transform while keeping a fixed frequency order.

evidence.quote: we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Two forward synthetic transforms, polynomial products of each record by signed packing, and the opposite transform consuming the same stored frequency order give the normalized ring convolution.

evidence.quote: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product

concepts.name: Exact recovery by rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Scaling out the known normalizations, showing the total coefficient error is below 1/2, rounding to integers and propagating radix carries yields the exact 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product.

concepts.name: The multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: Digits are placed on prime axes by the CRT map, transformed by Gaussian-resampled, chirped, synthetic transforms, multiplied pointwise, transformed back, rescaled, rounded and carried to give the exact product.

evidence.quote: The source-transform procedures now supply the three transforms needed for the radix-digit convolution.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication below n log n
concepts.gloss: A deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine that multiplies n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) time with κ = 2^{−182}, refuting the n log n optimality conjecture by replacing address rearrangement and Fourier layers with faster recursive tape procedures.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time
